transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-05
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Miguel (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Aisha (Head of ML, Silverline), Tom (VP Eng), Marta (Security Lead), Devon (Cloud Ops)

Summary: quick renewal and expansion check-in. customer asked about adding capacity and launching in EU region, plus contract extension options and SSO/KMS questions. Redwood to provide quote and schedule deeper architecture session.

Topics: renewal timing, dedicated capacity, additional regions (EU-west), data residency, SLAs, pricing, benchmarks, security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick agenda - renewal timeline, capacity needs, regional expansion, and any security questions. Aisha, do you want to kick off with current usage?
[00:18] Aisha: Yeah thanks Lena. so we've been seeing steady growth since the pilot, usage up about 3x qtr over qtr, our chat assistant is the big driver. latency's fine in us-west but once we route to eu it's pretty bad, and cost is creeping up with the current hosted model.
[00:34] Tom: to add, we're planning a product launch in EU in Q4 and need both lower latency and data residency controls. also want predictable monthly spend not surprise spikes.
[00:45] Miguel: got it. sounds like this is classic dedicated + multi-region scenario. we can do dedicated GPU pools in us-west for baseline and add an eu-west pool for local inference, keeps latency low and meets residency.
[00:58] Marta: quick question on data residency - if we process in eu-west can you guarantee that logs and kv cache don't leave region? we need to meet EU data residency for a particular client.
[01:10] Priya: good Q. Redwood has private deployment options and VPC-based private infra - we can pin routing so eu requests stay in eu, and audit logs can be configured to retain in-region. we'll share the specific docs after the call.
[01:22] Devon: network wise we need to know peering windows and any fixed egress charges. our cloud ops team will want to schedule maintenance windows for peering.
[01:30] Miguel: we'll document peering steps; egress depends on your cloud provider, but we can estimate in the quote. also for throughput: are you looking at steady 500 rps with bursts to 1k?
[01:42] Aisha: roughly that. current app profile is mid-sized requests - avg seq length about 512 tokens; a few endpoints use longer contexts up to 2k.
[01:52] Lena: on the contract side, I know the renewal is up end of august; would you prefer a 12-month extension with reserved dedicated nodes, or a hybrid reserved + burst plan?
[02:03] Tom: 12 months makes sense given product roadmap. we want committed capacity for baseline and some burst capacity to handle spikes. Also interested in pricing for adding the EU region as an add-on.
[02:15] Lena: perfect. i'll prepare a renewal quote that includes a 12-month commit for X dedicated GPUs, plus pricing for an eu-west pool as an optional add-on.
[02:24] Marta: also need to confirm KMS/HSM integration - can you support customer-managed keys for model logs and S3 at rest?
[02:33] Miguel: yes, we support KMS and HSM integrations for private deployments and Dedicated customers; there are some limitations for hosted tiers but with Dedicated or Private you'll get customer-managed key options. we'll share the integration guide.
[02:45] Aisha: one more thing - model fallback. if dedicated pool is saturated do you have auto-fallback to hosted or cheaper variants? we want graceful degradation, not 500s.
[02:56] Priya: yes, Redwood has routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or hosted capacity. latency SLOs vary but fallback is designed to keep responses available. we can show you the routing policy config in the console.
[03:10] Tom: about benchmarks - can you show expected p95 latency at our projected load? we plan to run a benchmark next week.
[03:18] Miguel: absolutely. i'll run a throughput profile with your avg sequence len 512 and the longer ones mixed in. i'll provide expected p50/p95 and token cost estimates.
[03:28] Devon: Regarding VPC peering, are there any special firewall ports or protocols required? also do we need to open anything for KV cache?
[03:36] Miguel: standard outbound HTTPS and a few internal ports for health checks; KV cache traffic is internal to the region when using dedicated pools, we'll document exact ports.
[03:45] Marta: security audit - we need SOC2 Type II report and ISO certs. can you provide a timeline for sharing?
[03:52] Priya: we can share SOC2 artifacts and ISO certs within 48 hours after this call and provide a point of contact for any follow ups.
[04:00] Aisha: cost - we need clear unit economics. can you give an example of cost per 1M tokens on dedicated vs hosted?
[04:09] Lena: i'll include a cost comparison in the quote. generally dedicated gives lower per-token cost at scale due to reserved capacity and better batching; we'll show model-quantization recommendations too.
[04:20] Tom: for the eu rollout timeline, if we sign an extension by mid-august can you have eu pool live by end of september?
[04:29] Miguel: plausible. depends on region capacity; we'll check GPU availability and can do a canary rollout - smaller pool first, then increase. i'll flag capacity procurement as an action item.
[04:38] Aisha: ok good. we also need a clause in the contract for SLA credits and uptime targets for dedicated nodes.
[04:46] Lena: we'll include SLA language in the quote and call out latency SLOs and remediation.
[04:52] Marta: one more compliance nuance - some logs must be redacted for certain EU customers. can you support field-level redaction before retention?
[05:02] Miguel: yes, we have hooks to redact or mask PII at ingestion in the private flow; we'll share sample configs.
[05:10] Tom: anything else?
[05:13] Aisha: hmm, just to confirm next steps: updated quote, security docs, architecture deep-dive, benchmark results.
[05:20] Lena: yep, that's it. we'll get the quote out by friday, miguel will run benchmarks and share by next tuesday, and we'll schedule an architecture deep dive for next week.
[05:30] Priya: i'll send calendar invites after the call for the deep-dive and make sure the right SE and our solutions engineering are on it.

Wrap-up/Recap:
- Redwood to send 12-month renewal quote with dedicated GPU commit and EU add-on pricing.
- SE to perform throughput benchmark (p50/p95) with Silverline's profile and share token cost estimates.
- Security docs (SOC2/ISO/KMS guide) to be shared within 48 hours.
- Customer to confirm GPU counts and region preference by 2026-08-12.

Links/shared artifacts mentioned: renewal quote (to be shared), SOC2/ISO artifacts (links to be sent), KMS integration guide (doc), benchmark spreadsheet (SE to share).

End of transcript.
